questions.q: What is the core difference between the push-based deploys in earlier lessons and GitOps?
options: In GitOps, a controller inside the cluster pulls changes from Git, instead of CI pushing changes into the cluster with stored credentials
GitOps eliminates the need for a container registry entirely
GitOps means developers deploy by SSHing directly into cluster nodes
There is no real difference — GitOps is just a rebranding of kubectl apply
questions.explain: Push means CI holds cluster credentials and runs kubectl/helm directly. Pull (GitOps) means a controller already running in the cluster watches Git and reconciles state on its own.

questions.q: In a GitOps pipeline, what does CI do differently at the end of the build, compared to the push-based pipeline from the previous lesson?
options: It commits the new image tag to a separate manifest repository instead of running kubectl or helm against the cluster directly
It deletes the Kubernetes cluster and recreates it
It emails the platform team to manually update the cluster
Nothing changes — CI's job is identical in both models
questions.explain: CI still builds and pushes the image, but instead of applying changes to the cluster itself, it commits the new tag to a manifest repo that the GitOps controller watches.

questions.q: What does `selfHeal: true` do in an Argo CD Application's sync policy?
options: Automatically reverts any manual, out-of-band change made directly in the cluster back to what's committed in Git
Automatically restarts any pod that crashes, regardless of its configuration
Automatically upgrades Argo CD itself to the latest version
Automatically deletes the Application resource after each sync
questions.explain: selfHeal makes Argo CD continuously enforce that the live cluster state matches Git, undoing any drift introduced outside of Git.

questions.q: In the Argo CD UI, what is the difference between an application being "Synced" and being "Healthy"?
options: Synced means the cluster's resources match what's in Git right now; Healthy means those resources are actually running correctly
They mean exactly the same thing and always change together
Synced refers to the Git repository's internet connection; Healthy refers to Argo CD's own server uptime
Healthy means Git matches the cluster; Synced means the pods are running
questions.explain: These are two independent signals — a deploy can briefly be Synced but not yet Healthy while new pods start, for example.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the main practical difference between Argo CD and Flux?
options: Argo CD bundles a full web UI and an explicit Application resource; Flux is UI-less by default and leans on Kustomization/HelmRelease resources — both follow the same pull-based pattern
Flux can only deploy to AWS, while Argo CD can only deploy to Google Cloud
Argo CD is a push-based tool while Flux is pull-based
Flux requires no Git repository at all
questions.explain: Both are CNCF graduated GitOps controllers solving the same problem; the differences are mostly about UI and resource shape, not the underlying pull-based model.
